pr.body:
Refs STREAM-266

Compression helped a lot bring the time on the main thread down. We now think we can scale down the consumers. However, we also need to ensure the flusher can keep up. So let's make the flusher spawn a process per redis shard. 

We think this is easier to do than making the process_spans/insert_spans multiprocessed. Over time we can offload mroe things like statistics/metrics to the flusher, and keep the main thread minimal.
pr.title: ref(span-buffer): Introduce multiprocessed flusher

raw_findings.body: `multiprocessing.Process` is `multiprocessing.context.Process`, while spawn-context children are `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`, which does not subclass it, so `isinstance(...)` is False and `kill()` is never called. The previous code killed the process unconditionally. The hung process keeps running and a second process is started for the same shards, producing duplicate segments to the buffered-segments topic and leaking processes on every restart.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Restart logic silently skips process termination, leaving duplicate/zombie flushers.
raw_findings.impact: `multiprocessing.Process` is `multiprocessing.context.Process`, while spawn-context children are `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`, which does not subclass it, so `isinstance(...)` is False and `kill()` is never called. The previous code killed the process unconditionally. The hung process keeps running and a second process is started for the same shards, producing duplicate segments to the buffered-segments topic and leaking processes on every restart.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new restart path added an `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard that does not match spawn-context process objects, replacing the previous unconditional kill.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Guard on the base class or capability instead, e.g. `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)` (or `hasattr(process, "kill")`), keeping the existing try/except for already-closed processes.
raw_findings.title: Hung flusher process is never killed because SpawnProcess is not an instance of multiprocessing.Process
raw_findings.trigger: A flusher child process (created via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`) hangs or stops updating `process_healthy_since`, so `_ensure_processes_alive()` detects cause="hang" and tries to restart it.

raw_findings.body: Unused code whose name differs from the live method by one character invites accidental calls to the wrong helper and adds maintenance burden with no coverage.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Dead, confusingly named code ships untested.
raw_findings.impact: Unused code whose name differs from the live method by one character invites accidental calls to the wrong helper and adds maintenance burden with no coverage.
raw_findings.root_cause: A per-shard restart helper was introduced during the multiprocess refactor but no caller was added.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Delete `_create_process_for_shard` (or wire it into a real restart-by-shard path if it is actually needed).
raw_findings.title: Dead helper `_create_process_for_shard` added but never called
raw_findings.trigger: Reading or maintaining the flusher: the repository-wide search shows no call site for `_create_process_for_shard` (singular); only `_create_process_for_shards` (plural) is used.

raw_findings.body: Documentation misstates the actual behavior for the default deployment configuration, misleading operators about parallelism and shard-to-process mapping.
raw_findings.evidence: Creates one process per shard for parallel processing.
raw_findings.impact: Documentation misstates the actual behavior for the default deployment configuration, misleading operators about parallelism and shard-to-process mapping.
raw_findings.root_cause: Docstring was written for the unbounded per-shard design while the implemented code caps processes with `max_processes`.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Reword to state that up to `max_processes` processes are created and shards are distributed round-robin across them, and document the new `max_processes` parameter in the docstring param list.
raw_findings.title: Class docstring claims one process per shard, contradicting the configurable max_processes (CLI default 1)
raw_findings.trigger: Running `sentry run consumer process-spans` without `--flusher-processes`: the new click option defaults to 1, so `max_processes=1` and `num_processes=min(1, len(shards))` yields a single process handling all shards.

raw_findings.body: Dashboards/alerts that group flusher metrics by a single tag key cannot join the two timers, and the mismatch looks like a typo to consumers of the metrics.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Metric tagging is inconsistent across sibling metrics in the same loop.
raw_findings.impact: Dashboards/alerts that group flusher metrics by a single tag key cannot join the two timers, and the mismatch looks like a typo to consumers of the metrics.
raw_findings.root_cause: Tag key was typed inconsistently when adding shard tags to the flusher metrics.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use the same tag key for both timers (e.g. `tags={"shard": shard_tag}` on `wait_produce`, matching `produce`).
raw_findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key: "shards" on wait_produce vs "shard" on the other flusher metrics
raw_findings.trigger: Any flush cycle emits `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` with tag key `shard` and `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` with tag key `shards`.

raw_findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` is incremented N times for one incident, inflating the counter by the shard fan-out and breaking existing alert thresholds tuned on the previous one-increment-per-detection semantics.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Health metric magnitude no longer corresponds to the number of incidents.
raw_findings.impact: `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` is incremented N times for one incident, inflating the counter by the shard fan-out and breaking existing alert thresholds tuned on the previous one-increment-per-detection semantics.
raw_findings.root_cause: The refactor fans a per-process health event out into one metric increment per owned shard.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Emit a single `metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy", tags={"cause": cause, "process_index": process_index})` per unhealthy process (optionally tagging the shard list) instead of looping over shards.
raw_findings.title: Unhealthy-flusher counter is now incremented once per shard instead of once per unhealthy process
raw_findings.trigger: A single flusher process that owns N shards (e.g. `--flusher-processes 1` with 8 assigned partitions) dies or hangs; `_ensure_processes_alive()` runs on the next `submit()`.

raw_findings.body: The loop breaks before reaching the remaining processes, so those processes are never terminated and keep flushing segments from Redis to Kafka while the consumer believes shutdown completed, risking concurrent flushers after rebalance/restart.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Shutdown path leaves child processes running when the join timeout elapses.
raw_findings.impact: The loop breaks before reaching the remaining processes, so those processes are never terminated and keep flushing segments from Redis to Kafka while the consumer believes shutdown completed, risking concurrent flushers after rebalance/restart.
raw_findings.root_cause: Deadline handling was placed as a loop-level `break` instead of only bounding the per-process wait.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Replace `break` with logic that still terminates every remaining process (e.g. skip the wait but always call terminate for each process, or terminate all processes after the wait loop ends).
raw_findings.title: join() breaks out of the whole loop on deadline expiry, skipping shutdown of remaining flusher processes
raw_findings.trigger: Consumer shutdown with a finite `timeout` where the first flusher process takes longer than the timeout to exit (e.g. it is stuck producing to Kafka) and more than one flusher process exists.

raw_findings.body: `SpansBuffer.flush_segments` computes `max_segments_per_shard = ceil(max_flush_segments / len(assigned_shards))` from the *subset*, so each of the N processes fetches up to `spans.buffer.max-flush-segments` segments per cycle; the cluster-wide flush rate becomes N× the configured option, increasing Redis and Kafka load beyond the intended cap and changing `any_shard_at_limit` backpressure sensitivity.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A configured global throughput limit is silently multiplied by the number of flusher processes.
raw_findings.impact: `SpansBuffer.flush_segments` computes `max_segments_per_shard = ceil(max_flush_segments / len(assigned_shards))` from the *subset*, so each of the N processes fetches up to `spans.buffer.max-flush-segments` segments per cycle; the cluster-wide flush rate becomes N× the configured option, increasing Redis and Kafka load beyond the intended cap and changing `any_shard_at_limit` backpressure sensitivity.
raw_findings.root_cause: Splitting the single buffer into per-process buffers changed the denominator used to derive the per-shard flush budget.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Scale the per-process budget explicitly (e.g. pass the total shard count / a per-process `max_flush_segments` derived from the global option) so the aggregate flush volume still honors `spans.buffer.max-flush-segments`.
raw_findings.title: Per-process SpansBuffer instances multiply the effective spans.buffer.max-flush-segments limit
raw_findings.trigger: Running with `--flusher-processes N` (N > 1) and M assigned shards, so each child buffer only knows M/N shards.

raw_findings.body: `get_memory_info()` returns cluster-wide usage via `iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client)`, so the same nodes are polled N times per submit; the used/available ratio is unchanged but N× the Redis INFO round trips are issued from the main thread on every submit.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Redundant Redis round trips on the hot consumer path.
raw_findings.impact: `get_memory_info()` returns cluster-wide usage via `iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client)`, so the same nodes are polled N times per submit; the used/available ratio is unchanged but N× the Redis INFO round trips are issued from the main thread on every submit.
raw_findings.root_cause: The per-shard buffer split was applied to a cluster-global memory query that is not shard-specific.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Query memory info from a single buffer (or a single shared Redis client) once per submit instead of iterating all per-process buffers.
raw_findings.title: Redis memory info is queried once per flusher buffer even though all buffers share the same cluster
raw_findings.trigger: `spans.buffer.max-memory-percentage` < 1.0 with `--flusher-processes N` (N > 1); every `submit()` call runs this loop.

raw_findings.body: With 0 the falsy check makes `max_processes` default to one process per shard — the opposite of the operator's intent to limit processes; with a negative value `num_processes` becomes negative, `process_to_shards_map` is empty, and `self.process_to_shards_map[i % num_processes]` raises KeyError, crashing consumer startup.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Invalid CLI input is silently reinterpreted or causes an unhandled KeyError.
raw_findings.impact: With 0 the falsy check makes `max_processes` default to one process per shard — the opposite of the operator's intent to limit processes; with a negative value `num_processes` becomes negative, `process_to_shards_map` is empty, and `self.process_to_shards_map[i % num_processes]` raises KeyError, crashing consumer startup.
raw_findings.root_cause: `or`-based defaulting conflates 0 with 'unset' and no lower bound is enforced on the new option.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Validate the value (e.g. `click.IntRange(min=1)` on the option and/or `if max_processes is not None and max_processes < 1: raise ValueError`) instead of relying on `or`.
raw_findings.title: Non-positive --flusher-processes is not validated and silently changes or breaks process allocation
raw_findings.trigger: Operator starts the consumer with `--flusher-processes 0` (or a negative value), which click accepts because the option only declares `type=int`.

raw_findings.body: The intended 100ms wait for the flusher thread never happens, so the comment is wrong and the assertion on `messages` depends on thread timing luck, making the test flaky (spurious `(msg,) = messages` unpacking failures in CI).
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test provides no actual synchronization and can fail nondeterministically.
raw_findings.impact: The intended 100ms wait for the flusher thread never happens, so the comment is wrong and the assertion on `messages` depends on thread timing luck, making the test flaky (spurious `(msg,) = messages` unpacking failures in CI).
raw_findings.root_cause: A synchronization sleep was added in a test that globally stubs out `time.sleep`.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use a real wait that bypasses the patch (capture `real_sleep = time.sleep` before monkeypatching, or poll for `messages` with a bounded timeout) instead of calling the patched `time.sleep`.
raw_findings.title: test_basic's added sleep is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched away
raw_findings.trigger: The test body starts with `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, which replaces the attribute on the `time` module that this line calls.

raw_findings.body: The core risk of this patch — spans landing on shards owned by a different flusher process and being flushed exactly once — is untested; a regression that drops or duplicates segments across per-shard buffers would still pass this test.
raw_findings.evidence:
total_shards = sum(len(shards) for shards in flusher.process_to_shards_map.values())
    assert total_shards == 4  # All 4 shards should be assigned
raw_findings.failure_mode: New parallel-flushing behavior ships without functional coverage.
raw_findings.impact: The core risk of this patch — spans landing on shards owned by a different flusher process and being flushed exactly once — is untested; a regression that drops or duplicates segments across per-shard buffers would still pass this test.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new test validates constructor bookkeeping rather than the end-to-end behavior the multiprocess flusher changes.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Extend the test to submit spans across the 4 partitions, advance `current_drift`, join, and assert every expected segment appears exactly once in `messages` (and that shards are distributed 2/2 across the two processes).
raw_findings.title: test_flusher_processes_limit asserts only internal counters, not that multi-process shard splitting still flushes segments
raw_findings.trigger: Running the new test: it never submits a span message, never advances `current_drift`, and never inspects `messages`.

finding.body: With 0 the falsy check makes `max_processes` default to one process per shard — the opposite of the operator's intent to limit processes; with a negative value `num_processes` becomes negative, `process_to_shards_map` is empty, and `self.process_to_shards_map[i % num_processes]` raises KeyError, crashing consumer startup.
finding.failure_mode: Invalid CLI input is silently reinterpreted or causes an unhandled KeyError.
finding.impact: With 0 the falsy check makes `max_processes` default to one process per shard — the opposite of the operator's intent to limit processes; with a negative value `num_processes` becomes negative, `process_to_shards_map` is empty, and `self.process_to_shards_map[i % num_processes]` raises KeyError, crashing consumer startup.
finding.root_cause: `or`-based defaulting conflates 0 with 'unset' and no lower bound is enforced on the new option.
finding.suggested_fix: Validate the value (e.g. `click.IntRange(min=1)` on the option and/or `if max_processes is not None and max_processes < 1: raise ValueError`) instead of relying on `or`.

finding.body: The intended 100ms wait for the flusher thread never happens, so the comment is wrong and the assertion on `messages` depends on thread timing luck, making the test flaky (spurious `(msg,) = messages` unpacking failures in CI).
finding.failure_mode: Test provides no actual synchronization and can fail nondeterministically.
finding.impact: The intended 100ms wait for the flusher thread never happens, so the comment is wrong and the assertion on `messages` depends on thread timing luck, making the test flaky (spurious `(msg,) = messages` unpacking failures in CI).
finding.root_cause: A synchronization sleep was added in a test that globally stubs out `time.sleep`.
finding.suggested_fix: Use a real wait that bypasses the patch (capture `real_sleep = time.sleep` before monkeypatching, or poll for `messages` with a bounded timeout) instead of calling the patched `time.sleep`.

validated_findings.body: `multiprocessing.Process` is `multiprocessing.context.Process`, while spawn-context children are `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`, which does not subclass it, so `isinstance(...)` is False and `kill()` is never called. The previous code killed the process unconditionally. The hung process keeps running and a second process is started for the same shards, producing duplicate segments to the buffered-segments topic and leaking processes on every restart.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Restart logic silently skips process termination, leaving duplicate/zombie flushers.
validated_findings.impact: `multiprocessing.Process` is `multiprocessing.context.Process`, while spawn-context children are `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`, which does not subclass it, so `isinstance(...)` is False and `kill()` is never called. The previous code killed the process unconditionally. The hung process keeps running and a second process is started for the same shards, producing duplicate segments to the buffered-segments topic and leaking processes on every restart.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new restart path added an `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` guard that does not match spawn-context process objects, replacing the previous unconditional kill.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Guard on the base class or capability instead, e.g. `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)` (or `hasattr(process, "kill")`), keeping the existing try/except for already-closed processes.
validated_findings.title: Hung flusher process is never killed because SpawnProcess is not an instance of multiprocessing.Process
validated_findings.trigger: A flusher child process (created via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`) hangs or stops updating `process_healthy_since`, so `_ensure_processes_alive()` detects cause="hang" and tries to restart it.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim is incorrect. In Python's multiprocessing module, `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` IS a subclass of `multiprocessing.Process` (which is `multiprocessing.context.Process`). The inheritance chain is SpawnProcess -> Process -> BaseProcess. The isinstance check will return True for spawn-context processes.

validated_findings.suggested_fix: Delete `_create_process_for_shard` (or wire it into a real restart-by-shard path if it is actually needed).

validated_findings.body: Documentation misstates the actual behavior for the default deployment configuration, misleading operators about parallelism and shard-to-process mapping.
validated_findings.evidence: Creates one process per shard for parallel processing.
validated_findings.impact: Documentation misstates the actual behavior for the default deployment configuration, misleading operators about parallelism and shard-to-process mapping.
validated_findings.root_cause: Docstring was written for the unbounded per-shard design while the implemented code caps processes with `max_processes`.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Reword to state that up to `max_processes` processes are created and shards are distributed round-robin across them, and document the new `max_processes` parameter in the docstring param list.
validated_findings.title: Class docstring claims one process per shard, contradicting the configurable max_processes (CLI default 1)
validated_findings.trigger: Running `sentry run consumer process-spans` without `--flusher-processes`: the new click option defaults to 1, so `max_processes=1` and `num_processes=min(1, len(shards))` yields a single process handling all shards.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 32 states 'Creates one process per shard for parallel processing' but line 51 shows `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and line 60 shows `min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`. With CLI default of 1 for flusher_processes, this creates 1 process for all shards, contradicting the docstring.

validated_findings.body: Dashboards/alerts that group flusher metrics by a single tag key cannot join the two timers, and the mismatch looks like a typo to consumers of the metrics.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Metric tagging is inconsistent across sibling metrics in the same loop.
validated_findings.impact: Dashboards/alerts that group flusher metrics by a single tag key cannot join the two timers, and the mismatch looks like a typo to consumers of the metrics.
validated_findings.root_cause: Tag key was typed inconsistently when adding shard tags to the flusher metrics.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use the same tag key for both timers (e.g. `tags={"shard": shard_tag}` on `wait_produce`, matching `produce`).
validated_findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key: "shards" on wait_produce vs "shard" on the other flusher metrics
validated_findings.trigger: Any flush cycle emits `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` with tag key `shard` and `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` with tag key `shards`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 199 shows `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` (plural) while line 185 shows `tags={"shard": shard_tag}` (singular). This is an inconsistent tag key that will cause metric aggregation issues.

validated_findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` is incremented N times for one incident, inflating the counter by the shard fan-out and breaking existing alert thresholds tuned on the previous one-increment-per-detection semantics.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Health metric magnitude no longer corresponds to the number of incidents.
validated_findings.impact: `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` is incremented N times for one incident, inflating the counter by the shard fan-out and breaking existing alert thresholds tuned on the previous one-increment-per-detection semantics.
validated_findings.root_cause: The refactor fans a per-process health event out into one metric increment per owned shard.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Emit a single `metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy", tags={"cause": cause, "process_index": process_index})` per unhealthy process (optionally tagging the shard list) instead of looping over shards.
validated_findings.title: Unhealthy-flusher counter is now incremented once per shard instead of once per unhealthy process
validated_findings.trigger: A single flusher process that owns N shards (e.g. `--flusher-processes 1` with 8 assigned partitions) dies or hangs; `_ensure_processes_alive()` runs on the next `submit()`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 242-245 show a loop `for shard in shards: metrics.incr(...)` which increments the unhealthy counter once per shard owned by the process. This changes the metric semantics from per-process to per-shard, potentially breaking existing alerts.

validated_findings.body: The loop breaks before reaching the remaining processes, so those processes are never terminated and keep flushing segments from Redis to Kafka while the consumer believes shutdown completed, risking concurrent flushers after rebalance/restart.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Shutdown path leaves child processes running when the join timeout elapses.
validated_findings.impact: The loop breaks before reaching the remaining processes, so those processes are never terminated and keep flushing segments from Redis to Kafka while the consumer believes shutdown completed, risking concurrent flushers after rebalance/restart.
validated_findings.root_cause: Deadline handling was placed as a loop-level `break` instead of only bounding the per-process wait.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Replace `break` with logic that still terminates every remaining process (e.g. skip the wait but always call terminate for each process, or terminate all processes after the wait loop ends).
validated_findings.title: join() breaks out of the whole loop on deadline expiry, skipping shutdown of remaining flusher processes
validated_findings.trigger: Consumer shutdown with a finite `timeout` where the first flusher process takes longer than the timeout to exit (e.g. it is stuck producing to Kafka) and more than one flusher process exists.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 338-341 show that when deadline expires (`remaining_time <= 0`), the code `break`s out of the entire process loop. Processes not yet iterated will never have `terminate()` called on them, leaving them running.

validated_findings.body: `SpansBuffer.flush_segments` computes `max_segments_per_shard = ceil(max_flush_segments / len(assigned_shards))` from the *subset*, so each of the N processes fetches up to `spans.buffer.max-flush-segments` segments per cycle; the cluster-wide flush rate becomes N× the configured option, increasing Redis and Kafka load beyond the intended cap and changing `any_shard_at_limit` backpressure sensitivity.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A configured global throughput limit is silently multiplied by the number of flusher processes.
validated_findings.impact: `SpansBuffer.flush_segments` computes `max_segments_per_shard = ceil(max_flush_segments / len(assigned_shards))` from the *subset*, so each of the N processes fetches up to `spans.buffer.max-flush-segments` segments per cycle; the cluster-wide flush rate becomes N× the configured option, increasing Redis and Kafka load beyond the intended cap and changing `any_shard_at_limit` backpressure sensitivity.
validated_findings.root_cause: Splitting the single buffer into per-process buffers changed the denominator used to derive the per-shard flush budget.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Scale the per-process budget explicitly (e.g. pass the total shard count / a per-process `max_flush_segments` derived from the global option) so the aggregate flush volume still honors `spans.buffer.max-flush-segments`.
validated_findings.title: Per-process SpansBuffer instances multiply the effective spans.buffer.max-flush-segments limit
validated_findings.trigger: Running with `--flusher-processes N` (N > 1) and M assigned shards, so each child buffer only knows M/N shards.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 93 creates `SpansBuffer(shards)` per process with only that process's shards. Since `flush_segments` uses `len(self.assigned_shards)` to compute `max_segments_per_shard`, each process will flush up to the full configured limit, multiplying total throughput by N processes.

validated_findings.body: `get_memory_info()` returns cluster-wide usage via `iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client)`, so the same nodes are polled N times per submit; the used/available ratio is unchanged but N× the Redis INFO round trips are issued from the main thread on every submit.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Redundant Redis round trips on the hot consumer path.
validated_findings.impact: `get_memory_info()` returns cluster-wide usage via `iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client)`, so the same nodes are polled N times per submit; the used/available ratio is unchanged but N× the Redis INFO round trips are issued from the main thread on every submit.
validated_findings.root_cause: The per-shard buffer split was applied to a cluster-global memory query that is not shard-specific.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Query memory info from a single buffer (or a single shared Redis client) once per submit instead of iterating all per-process buffers.
